story.title: Small Forces (Book One of The Drift Trilogy)
story.premise: In 2219 the Belt runs on water, credit and insurance. Piq Adebayo-Lund is a field assessor for the Assessment Office of the Ceres Mutual Assurance Compact. The Compact underwrites nearly every Belt habitat, and its actuaries are, in all but name, the Belt's intelligence service. Piq travels under a cover that is technically true: she holds a real Ceres Registry commission as a notary and marriage celebrant, and her notarial seal doubles as a Compact optical authentication key. She boards the Mars–Ceres cycler Patience with one job. The ship will fly past Vesta in 140 days, and she must confirm whether the Martian-aligned Vesta Works has built a mass driver to throw kinetic weapons at Ceres. Aboard she meets Teodora 'Teo' Anselm, the ship's trajectory and mass officer. Teo is careful, wry and quietly grieving, and she is the only person aboard who can read orbits the way Piq reads people. Piq mistakes a test flash for an attack and sends a report she cannot recall, at the speed of light. She and Teo then discover three things. The driver is not a weapon. The thing it is fighting was set loose by Ceres itself. And the 'confirmation' Piq sent has launched a silent interceptor that will destroy the only machine that can save her home. Stopping it means spending the water that shields them from the sun, aboard a small taxi with no way back, with the woman Piq has come to love beside her.
story.setting: The Main Asteroid Belt and inner Solar System, 2219. There is no faster-than-light travel or communication, and every plot beat respects it. Ceres is a cooperative of pressurized warrens and ice mines. Its wealth rests on water exports and on the Ceres Mutual Assurance Compact, which insures ships, habitats and cargo across the Belt. Vesta is a Mars Republic protectorate. Its Vesta Works industrial complex has built a 9-kilometre electromagnetic mass driver. Mars and Ceres are negotiating the Hygiea Water Accord, and leverage is everything. Most of the novel takes place aboard Patience, a 1.2-kilometre Mars–Belt cycler on a fixed free-return orbit. It rarely burns, because every kilogram of reaction mass is water that could be drunk, grown into food, or used as radiation shielding. Patience has a 1/3-g spin ring (hydroponics, cabins, a chapel-cum-courtroom), a microgravity hub (docks, mass office, telescope club), a water-walled storm shelter, and a single small taxi, the Gannet, with about 2.1 km/s of delta-v when fully fuelled. On this pass Patience sweeps within 40,000 km of Vesta. One-way light delay between the ship and Ceres runs 18 to 31 minutes as the geometry changes. Traffic from the ship's own high-gain dish travels direct. Everything else goes through the Pallas Relay, a bureaucratic store-and-forward station that batches low-priority traffic every 12 hours. Physics in play: orbital mechanics and launch windows; the Yarkovsky effect (sunlight re-radiated as heat gives a slow, steady thrust that drifts small asteroids over decades); kinetic deflection; solar particle events; Coriolis effects in the spin ring; mass budgets as moral choices.
story.tone: Close third person locked to Piq for the whole novel. The reader knows only what Piq perceives, infers or misreads, and that is how the twists play fair. Prose is vivid but economical: concrete sensory detail of life in microgravity and spin (the smell of recycled air and tomato vines, condensation beading on cold hull plates, the sideways tug of Coriolis when you stand up too fast), with no purple passages and no info-dumps. Hard science enters through character, as arguments over mass, jokes about delay, calculations scribbled on a wrist slate, and every physics fact the plot later depends on is shown on the page before it matters. Each chapter runs about 4,000 to 5,000 words, holds one clear dramatic movement, and ends with forward momentum: a new question, a reversal, a message arriving, a decision that cannot be unmade. The romance is a genuine slow burn. It runs on competence, shared problem-solving and honesty earned at cost: a hand steadied on a grab-rail, a first kiss in Chapter 16, and the choice made in Chapter 24. Comedy is frequent and situational, and it grows from the setting: cover identities colliding, microgravity mishaps, cycler bureaucracy, messages arriving in absurd clumps, plans that work for the wrong reason. Comedy dominates Chapters 1 to 8, threads through the middle, and is fully withdrawn from the climactic sequence (Chapters 18 to 22) except where a small human moment releases pressure without breaking suspense. It returns warmly in Chapter 24. Underneath the wit, the governing feeling is the ache of distance: everything you say arrives late, so you must decide who you are before you know how it lands.

characters.name: Piq Adebayo-Lund
characters.role: Protagonist. Ceres-born field assessor (intelligence officer) for the Assessment Office of the Ceres Mutual Assurance Compact, aged 34. Cover: a genuinely licensed traveling notary and marriage celebrant. Tall and low-g lean, sharp-tongued, very good at reading rooms and very bad at waiting.
characters.want: To close one clean, decisive mission that earns her a desk on Ceres and an end to living under covers. Beneath that, she wants to be known by someone as who she actually is rather than who she is pretending to be.
characters.flaw: Impatience disguised as decisiveness. In a universe where every message is late, she acts before confirmation, trusts her read of people over the physics of the situation, and treats her own feelings as an operational liability to be managed rather than told.

characters.name: Teodora 'Teo' Anselm
characters.role: Love interest. Trajectory and mass officer of the cycler Patience, aged 38. Mars-born daughter of a Belter tug pilot. Weighs every passenger and parcel, plots every flyby, and runs the ship's mass budget with dry humor and absolute precision. She is not an agent of anyone and never deceives Piq.
characters.want: To clear the name of her late mother, Renata Anselm. Renata was blamed in a Ceres Mutual claim for a tug incident 31 years ago and died never having been believed. Teo also wants to stay aboard Patience, whose fixed orbit is the only place she has ever felt safe.
characters.flaw: Retreats into calculation whenever a risk cannot be quantified. She will not make choices whose outcomes she cannot model, which includes loving someone whose job is lying, and leaving the ship.

characters.name: Marisol Quah
characters.role: Piq's handler and head of field assessment at Ceres Mutual, aged 63. Seen only through light-delayed messages that arrive 18 to 31 minutes after they were sent, and sometimes in batches. Honest and protective.
characters.want: To keep Ceres safe and to keep the Compact's board from using the Assessment Office as a weapon.
characters.flaw: Faith in protocol. She writes terse, compressed messages built for security, never stopping to consider how they will read after a half-hour delay and out of order.

characters.name: Dr. Iskander Vell
characters.role: Chief engineer of the Vesta Works mass driver. A brilliant, proud, lonely man running a secret deflection campaign against the orders of his Martian superiors.
characters.want: To push the asteroid Lantern off its path toward Ceres without anyone knowing, so Mars cannot use the threat as leverage and Ceres never has to be afraid.
characters.flaw: Secrecy as pride. He would rather save people alone and in silence than ask for help, and that silence is what makes his driver look like a weapon.

characters.name: Attaché Dace Ruiz
characters.role: Mars Republic diplomatic attaché traveling openly aboard Patience on the way to the Hygiea Water Accord talks. Courteous, legalistic, and openly hunting for the Ceres assessor he knows is aboard. He never pretends to be anything other than what he is.
characters.want: To carry the Lantern secret to the treaty table intact, as Mars's decisive leverage over Ceres's water rights.
characters.flaw: He mistakes leverage for security, and he is too proud of his own correctness to notice when the facts change under him.

characters.name: Brother Lennart Ostlund
characters.role: Comic foil turned ally. A real, deeply pedantic traveling celebrant of the Fellowship of the Long Orbit. He is outraged to share a ship with a competing celebrant and audits Piq's credentials with forensic zeal.
characters.want: To protect the dignity of his vocation and to officiate the cycler's 'wedding of the season'.
characters.flaw: Pedantry so total that he cannot let a single improperly filed form pass, even when that is inconvenient for everyone, including himself.

characters.name: Captain Ama Okonkwo-Reyes
characters.role: Master of Patience. Even-handed, unflappable, and fiercely protective of the ship's water.
characters.want: To bring every soul aboard home on a mass budget with no slack in it.
characters.flaw: Reads every request as a mass problem first and a human problem second.

characters.name: Juniper Haldane-Szabo
characters.role: A 15-year-old passenger who runs the ship's telescope club and an illegal betting pool on Vesta 'flash' sightings. A meticulous, mercenary record-keeper.
characters.want: To win the pool, and to be taken seriously as an observer by an adult.
characters.flaw: Monetizes everything and trusts no one who won't put stakes down.

story.arc:
ACT ONE: COVER (Chapters 1–8). Ch1: Piq boards Patience from a Mars-flyby taxi carrying 14 kg of luggage over her mass allowance. Teo weighs her in the oscillating inertial-mass chair and offers two options: pay per kilogram, or wear it. Piq spends the chapter in five layers of clothing. Her mission brief from Marisol: image and characterize the Vesta driver before the flyby in 140 days and confirm or deny a threat to Ceres. Ends: within six hours of boarding, a passenger couple, Halvard and Mei-Lin, book Piq to marry them. She has never officiated anything. Ch2: Brother Ostlund discovers another celebrant aboard and opens a formal audit of her license. Piq's mother's chatty messages arrive in absurd clumps of eight every 12 hours, routed through the Pallas Relay's low-priority batch queue (clue for Twist 3). Ostlund pedantically notes that Piq's seal stamps times a few seconds off ship's clock (clue for the climax). Ruiz introduces himself at dinner and announces, pleasantly, that he knows Ceres has an assessor aboard. Ends: Piq learns that time on the ship's high-gain dish is rationed by the captain, and Vesta enters telescope range. Ch3: Piq joins Juniper's telescope club as cover and images the driver. Teo, the club's reluctant sponsor, remarks that the rail's orientation is 'a weird way to aim at anything in the ecliptic' (Twist 1 clue). Wedding rehearsal in the spin ring: everyone walks into walls from Coriolis. Ends: the first flash, a driver launch, blooms on the screen. Ch4: A storm-shelter drill crams 140 people into the water-walled shelter. Teo explains that the ship's water is shield, drinking supply and propellant all at once, so spending one means losing the others (climax seed). Ostlund, to spite Piq, tries to marry Halvard and Mei-Lin in the shelter. Juniper's pool logs exact flash times (Twist 1 clue). Ends: Marisol's message arrives: 'Quiet Option fuelled. Confirm or deny within window.' Ch5: Among the cover documents Piq is notarizing for passengers is an old Ceres Mutual claim file for a 31-year-old tug 'parking' operation on a small rubble-pile asteroid, designation 2188 KR, which records spoil being dumped onto it. The pilot of record is Renata Anselm (Twist 2 clue). Ends: a second flash, timed when Piq believes Ceres is in the firing line. Ch6: Under the deadline, Piq sends 'Weapon live. Driver active against Ceres' over the dish on priority. That evening Teo explains the Yarkovsky effect with a joke about sunbathers drifting off the beach: dark rocks warm, re-radiate heat, and creep across the sky over decades (Twist 2 clue). Ends: Teo, intrigued by the flash, asks to see Piq's data. Ch7: Piq's first zero-g wedding goes gloriously wrong when the rings drift into an air-return filter. She retrieves them and the vows hold. Teo tells Piq about her mother, who was disgraced by an insurer's ruling. Their first real dinner together. Ends: Ruiz corners Piq. He doesn't know it is her, but he is narrowing the field. Ch8: Teo and Piq overlay Juniper's flash times against the true geometry. The launch windows never match Ceres. Juniper mentions a faint 'ghost' smudge in her survey plates that she has written off (Twist 3 clue). Ends: Teo back-solves the projectiles' destination to a small body, 2188 KR.

ACT TWO: DRIFT (Chapters 9–17). Ch9, TWIST 1: The driver is not a weapon. It is firing payloads into 2188 KR, which Vesta has nicknamed 'Lantern', to deflect it, because Lantern is drifting onto a path that meets Ceres in nine years. Everything Piq read as aggression was rescue. Her report was wrong. The dish is locked to Ruiz's treaty traffic and a scheduled antenna-calibration window, so she sends a retraction through the Pallas Relay on her notarial commercial account, which the relay classes as low priority. Ends: Piq tells Teo the truth about her job. Teo leaves without a word. Ch10: Teo is hurt and withdrawn. Ostlund files a complaint that drags Piq before the ship's administrative hearing. Teo finds that Lantern's albedo is far darker than its original catalog entry (Twist 2 clue). Ends: Teo knocks on Piq's door. 'I need someone who can read insurance claims.' The catalog lists Lantern's parking pilot as Renata Anselm. Ch11: At the hearing, Piq's license proves entirely valid. Ostlund is mortified, then becomes a grudging ally. A plan that works for the wrong reason: his complaint triggers an audit that frees up dish time, though not soon enough to matter. Piq glances at the Pallas batch schedule in the comms log without registering what it means (Twist 3 clue). Romance deepens among the hydroponics vines. Ends: Marisol's reply: 'Received. Proceeding.' Piq reads 'proceeding' as 'proceeding with analysis'. Ch12: Teo and Piq rebuild the 31-year history. Mining spoil darkened Lantern's surface, and the Yarkovsky drift has been working on it ever since. Ruiz openly confirms that Mars knows about Lantern and intends to use it at the Accord. Ends: Vell tight-beams Patience and asks for Teo by name, because he needs her mother's original logs. Ch13: A conversation with Vell on a nine-minute round-trip delay, played as both comedy and tension: answers keep arriving to questions already abandoned. Vell confesses he is deflecting Lantern alone, against Martian orders. An almost-kiss. Ends: Teo opens her mother's personal archive. Ch14, TWIST 2: Renata's logs show she obeyed a Ceres Mutual directive to park Lantern and coat it with spoil, and that she formally warned it would change the rock's thermal behaviour. The Compact closed her warning and blamed her instead for an unrelated docking mishap. Ceres created its own doomsday rock, and Vesta is quietly saving Ceres from it. Ends: Piq finds the sanitized file's authorising signature. It is a board-level initial set she cannot identify. Ch15: Grief and tenderness between Piq and Teo. The captain announces a water leak and rations. Marisol sends 'QO coast nominal', which Piq misses in a clump of her mother's messages. Ends: Ruiz identifies Piq and invokes ship's law to have her confined. Ch16: Piq is confined to her cabin, the captain refusing to take sides. Ostlund smuggles notes to her inside wedding paperwork. First kiss, through the open hatch, when Teo visits. Ends: together they finally parse 'QO coast nominal': something launched is now coasting. Ch17: Teo re-reduces Juniper's 'ghost' images and finds a dim object on the Ceres–Vesta line. Ends: Piq lines up the launch timestamp against the moment her retraction left the ship.

ACT THREE: THE COST OF MASS (Chapters 18–24). Ch18, TWIST 3: Her retraction sat in the Pallas batch queue for 11 hours. It reached Ceres after the decision window had closed, and the Quiet Option was launched on her first report. Nobody lied: Marisol acted correctly on what she had. The interceptor is a dark kinetic penetrator, radio-silent so it cannot be spoofed and abortable only by an optical key at close range. Its target is the driver. Without the driver's final shots, Lantern hits Ceres. Ends: the interceptor reaches Vesta in 26 days, and Patience flies past in 22. Ch19: The only key within reach is Piq's notary seal. The only vehicle is the Gannet. Its propellant is water. The captain refuses. The passengers, led by Ostlund and the newlyweds, donate their water rations. Ruiz moves to block the launch until Piq points out that a destroyed driver costs Mars its leverage too. He stands aside for the wrong reason. Ends: a solar particle event is forecast. Ch20: Teo insists on flying the intercept, knowing that leaving Patience means not returning for years. Launch. Ends: the solar particle event arrives early. Ch21: No comedy. In the Gannet, every kilogram of water they burn is a kilogram less shielding. Teo calculates radiation dose against delta-v in real time while Piq keeps her talking. Ends: they acquire the interceptor optically, and it is not where it should be. Ch22: The interceptor has made a terminal correction. They overburn and take more dose. At 900 km the seal's handshake fails because its clock drift, planted in Chapter 2, throws off the timing. Piq corrects it using light-delay arithmetic Teo taught her. The abort succeeds. Ends: the Gannet no longer has the propellant to return to Patience and is falling toward Vesta in the driver's final firing window. Ch23: Vell fires the last rounds. Teo's tracking confirms Lantern is deflected clear of Ceres. A Vesta tug captures the Gannet. Vell publicly confesses the deflection campaign and the cover-up he uncovered, and accepts arrest by Mars. Ends: Teo's final track shows a small fragment shed by the last impact. Ch24: Aftermath on Vesta. Piq notarizes Renata's logs into the public record, clearing her name. Marisol's message arrives with apology, thanks and a summons. Piq and Teo, both with radiation dose and both stranded nine months from the next transfer window, choose each other plainly and without any cover. Their future is uncertain: inquiries, Martian jurisdiction, careers in ruins. Final image: two women watching Ceres, a bright point 31 light-minutes away, talking about what they will say when they get there.

RESOLVED BY THE FINAL CHAPTER: the mission and its central mystery (the driver's true purpose, Lantern's origin, the launch of the Quiet Option); Lantern's deflection; the romance; Teo's mother's name; and every subplot listed below.

Deliberate trilogy hooks, left open on purpose: (1) The fragment 'Wick'. The final impact shed a boulder whose orbit cannot yet be determined. Seeded by Teo's Chapter 6 lecture on rubble piles and Vell's Chapter 13 warning that a final hard push risks fragmentation. Its threat stays unknown for years. (2) The board initials. Someone on the Ceres Mutual board signed the sanitized Lantern claim 31 years ago and approved the Quiet Option's standing protocol. Seeded in Chapters 5, 14 and 15. Marisol's final message promises an 'internal' inquiry, and the signer remains unnamed. (3) Mars holds the driver. With Vell in custody, the Mars Republic now owns a combat-proven long-range kinetic system. Ruiz's honest report has named Piq, burning her cover, and she is summoned to the Hygiea Water Accord talks at Mars. Seeded by Ruiz's openly stated mission and by Vell's Chapter 13 remark that 'anything that can push a mountain can throw one.'
subplots: The celebrant war: Brother Ostlund's audit and complaint against Piq. It begins as pure comedy, peaks in the Chapter 11 hearing where her commission proves genuine, and turns to alliance: he smuggles her notes, leads the water donation, and in Chapter 24 officiates the vow-renewal of Halvard and Mei-Lin, whose first wedding Piq performed. Fully resolved.

Teo's mother: Renata Anselm's disgrace, its discovery in Piq's cover paperwork, the archive reveal, and her exoneration when Piq notarizes the logs into the public record. This subplot carries Twist 2 and makes the romance a shared cause. Fully resolved.

Juniper's flash pool: the illegal betting pool whose records crack Twist 1 and whose 'ghost' smudge cracks Twist 3. Juniper wins the pool, and in Chapter 24 Vell's team cites her as a credited observer. Fully resolved.

The mass budget: Captain Okonkwo-Reyes's water rationing, the leak, the passengers' donated water, and the Gannet's spent propellant. Vesta repays the ship's water in full as part of Vell's public confession. Fully resolved.

Attaché Ruiz: his open hunt for the Ceres assessor, Piq's confinement, and his decision to step aside for self-interested reasons. In Chapter 23 he places the true sequence of events on the record honestly, which closes his personal arc while the geopolitical fallout is reserved as a trilogy hook.

Piq's mother's messages: absurdly cheerful clumps of mail that arrive every 12 hours through the Pallas Relay, a running joke that is also the key clue to Twist 3. After the climax Piq finally sends her mother something true, that she has fallen in love. The reply arrives in Chapter 24 in a clump of eleven messages, the last of which simply says 'Bring her home.' Fully resolved.

Marisol and the Office: their light-delayed working relationship, the misread 'Proceeding' and 'QO coast nominal' messages, and Marisol's final message of apology, thanks and summons, which settles the trust between handler and agent. Fully resolved; only the board signer is reserved as a trilogy hook.

Vell's secret campaign: his lonely deflection effort, his delayed conversations with Teo, and his public confession and arrest. Vell's personal arc is closed; what Mars does with the driver is reserved as a trilogy hook.

outline.summary: Piq Adebayo-Lund comes aboard the cycler Patience from a Mars-flyby taxi with 14 kg of luggage over her mass allowance. In the hub mass office, trajectory and mass officer Teo Anselm weighs her in the oscillating inertial-mass chair, a microgravity scale that times how fast she bobs. Teo dryly offers two options: pay per kilogram, or wear it. Piq is too proud to pay and too stubborn to repack, so she spends the chapter in five layers of clothing, sweating through orientation in the spin ring. The sideways tug of Coriolis catches her whenever she stands too fast, and the corridors smell of recycled air and tomato vines. Close third person establishes her cover, which is technically true: she is a genuinely licensed Ceres Registry notary and marriage celebrant, and her notarial seal doubles as a Compact optical authentication key. Alone in her cabin she plays Marisol Quah's compressed mission brief. Patience flies past Vesta in 140 days, and Piq must image and characterize the Vesta Works mass driver and confirm or deny whether it threatens Ceres. A clean result means a desk on Ceres and no more covers. Within six hours of boarding, the passenger couple Halvard and Mei-Lin find her listing in the ship directory and book her to marry them. Piq has never officiated anything in her life, and she says yes.

Brother Lennart Ostlund of the Fellowship of the Long Orbit learns that a rival celebrant is aboard. He arrives with forms and opens a formal audit of Piq's license. While inspecting her stamped paperwork he pedantically points out that her seal's timestamps run a few seconds off ship's clock. He demands she log it, and Piq waves it away. Her mother's chatty messages then arrive in an absurd clump of eight at once, about recipes, a neighbour's hip and a cat. Teo, amused, explains that commercial and personal mail goes through the Pallas Relay, which batches low-priority traffic every 12 hours, while only the ship's own high-gain dish sends direct. The two of them trade jokes about light delay: one-way lag to Ceres runs 18 to 31 minutes, so every argument is won by whoever stops talking first. At dinner Mars Republic attaché Dace Ruiz, travelling openly to the Hygiea Water Accord talks, introduces himself courteously to the table. He announces, pleasantly, that he knows Ceres has an assessor aboard and looks forward to meeting them properly. Piq keeps her face still while Ostlund loudly demands her license number. Ends: Piq learns that Captain Okonkwo-Reyes rations time on the high-gain dish, and that Vesta has just come into telescope range.

Piq needs telescope access as cover, so she joins the ship's telescope club. It is run by fifteen-year-old Juniper Haldane-Szabo, who also runs an illegal betting pool on Vesta 'flash' sightings and demands Piq buy in before she may touch an eyepiece. Teo is the club's reluctant sponsor. As Piq images the 9-kilometre rail of the driver, Teo idly remarks that its orientation is 'a weird way to aim at anything in the ecliptic'. Piq files the comment as trivia. That evening, the wedding rehearsal in the spin-ring chapel, which doubles as the ship's courtroom, becomes a set piece of Coriolis comedy. The bridal party veers into walls, Mei-Lin's mother drifts sideways down the aisle, and Ostlund attends uninvited to take notes on Piq's procedural errors. Teo, roped in as witness, steadies Piq's hand on a grab-rail, and Piq notices she noticed. Ends: back at the telescope, the first flash blooms on the screen, a bright pulse from the driver's muzzle, and Juniper calmly logs the exact time while Piq's pulse spikes.

A storm-shelter drill crams 140 people into the water-walled shelter. Teo explains, with a mass officer's gallows wit, that the ship's water is shielding, drinking supply and propellant all at once, so spending one means losing the others. She mentions that the ship's lone taxi, the Gannet, carries about 2.1 km/s of delta-v fully fuelled and burns that same water, and that a solar particle event can arrive with little warning. To spite Piq, Ostlund tries to marry Halvard and Mei-Lin on the spot in the shelter, and the result is bureaucratic farce. Juniper works the crowd, collecting bets and showing Piq her meticulous log of exact flash times. Afterward Piq works through a stack of passenger documents to keep her cover warm. Among them is an old Ceres Mutual claim file a passenger needs notarized: a 31-year-old tug 'parking' operation on a small rubble-pile asteroid, designation 2188 KR. The file records mining spoil being dumped onto the rock, a board-level sign-off, and a pilot of record named Renata Anselm. Piq registers the surname but has no context yet and sets the file aside. Ends: Marisol's message arrives: 'Quiet Option fuelled. Confirm or deny within window.' Minutes later a second flash comes, timed at a moment when Piq's rough geometry puts Ceres in the firing line.

With the deadline on her and the flashes seeming to fit, Piq argues herself into certainty. She trusts her read of the situation over the physics she hasn't checked. She bargains for a priority slot on the dish and sends 'Weapon live. Driver active against Ceres'. Once sent it cannot be recalled, and she counts out the minutes it takes to reach Ceres. That evening Teo explains the Yarkovsky effect with a joke about sunbathers drifting off the beach: dark rocks warm, re-radiate heat, and creep across the sky over decades. She adds that rubble piles are loose bags of gravel that can shed boulders if pushed too hard. Piq's first real wedding follows in the zero-g hub. It goes gloriously wrong when the rings drift into an air-return filter, and Piq retrieves them upside-down with the whole party cheering. The vows hold. At the reception the comedy softens into the first real dinner between Piq and Teo, who tells her about her mother. Renata was a Belter tug pilot disgraced by an insurer's ruling over a docking mishap, and she died never having been believed. Piq remembers the name on the claim file and says nothing. Teo, intrigued by the flash, asks to see Piq's telescope data. Ends: Ruiz corners Piq in the corridor. He doesn't know it is her, but he lists the passengers he has already ruled out, and she is on a very short list.

Piq shares the data with Teo under cover of the telescope club, half hoping Teo will confirm the threat and half dreading it. In the mass office they overlay Juniper's exact flash times against the true orbital geometry, and the comedy is in Teo's quiet, devastating corrections of Piq's back-of-envelope sketches. The launch windows never line up with Ceres, not once. Juniper wants proof the adults are taking her seriously before she shares her full survey, so she makes them stake credit. She then mentions in passing a faint 'ghost' smudge on several survey plates, which she wrote off as a sensor artefact and refuses to waste a bet on. Piq barely glances at it. Teo works through the night on her wrist slate, back-solving the projectiles' trajectories, and Piq watches her pull the answer out of the dark. Ends: the shots converge on a small body, 2188 KR, the rock in the claim file with Renata Anselm's name on it.

TWIST 1. Teo's model, cross-checked against Juniper's records, shows the driver is not a weapon. It is firing payloads into 2188 KR, which Vesta has nicknamed 'Lantern', to deflect it, because Lantern is drifting onto a path that meets Ceres in nine years. The odd rail orientation, the flash timings and the windows that never matched Ceres all now read as rescue. Piq's report was wrong, and Marisol warned that the Quiet Option was fuelled. Piq races to retract. The dish is locked to Ruiz's treaty traffic and a scheduled antenna-calibration window, and Piq cannot request priority without exposing herself to Ruiz. So she sends the retraction through the Pallas Relay on her notarial commercial account, which the relay classes as low priority. She tells herself it will arrive in time. Then, because Teo did the work and deserves it, Piq tells her the truth: she is a Compact field assessor, and the notary cover is real but it is still a cover. Ends: Teo looks at her for a long moment and leaves the mass office without a word.

Teo is hurt and withdrawn, answering Piq only in mass-budget formalities. Ostlund's complaint against Piq's credentials now drags her before the ship's administrative hearing in the chapel-courtroom, and the reader feels the danger that scrutiny could break her cover in front of Ruiz. Juniper relays, for a fee, that Teo has been in the observatory all night and has found Lantern's albedo far darker than its original catalog entry. At the hearing Piq's commission proves entirely valid, down to the stamp and registry seal. Ostlund is mortified, then becomes a grudging, pedantic ally. His complaint has also triggered an audit that frees up dish time, a plan that works for the wrong reason, though not soon enough to matter. Reviewing the comms log for the hearing, Piq glances at the Pallas batch schedule and its 12-hour cycle without registering what it means for her retraction. Ends: Teo knocks on Piq's door. 'I need someone who can read insurance claims.' The original catalog lists Lantern's parking pilot as Renata Anselm.

An uneasy partnership forms among the hydroponics vines, where it is warm and condensation beads on the cold hull plates. Piq brings out the claim file and they rebuild the 31-year history together. Mining spoil darkened Lantern's surface, the darker rock absorbs more sunlight, and the Yarkovsky drift Teo joked about has been pushing it ever since. They argue, laugh and fall into rhythm, and the romance deepens through competence and honesty. Ruiz finds them and makes no secret of his position: Mars knows about Lantern and intends to use it at the Accord as leverage over Ceres's water rights. Marisol's reply arrives: 'Received. Proceeding.' Piq reads 'proceeding' as 'proceeding with analysis' and lets herself breathe. Ends: Dr. Iskander Vell, chief engineer of the Vesta Works driver, tight-beams Patience and asks for Teo by name, because he needs her mother's original logs.

Piq and Teo hold a conversation with Vell on a nine-minute round-trip delay, played as both comedy and tension. Answers keep arriving to questions already abandoned, Vell pre-empts objections nobody raised, and Teo teaches Piq to keep the light-delay arithmetic straight on her wrist slate, tracking who knew what when. Vell confesses that he is deflecting Lantern alone, against Martian orders, so Mars cannot use the threat and Ceres never has to be afraid. He warns that a final hard push risks fragmenting the rubble pile. He also remarks, almost to himself, that 'anything that can push a mountain can throw one.' After the link closes, Piq and Teo are alone in the mass office and nearly kiss, and Teo pulls back into calculation. Ends: Teo opens her mother's personal archive, which she has carried for decades and never been able to read.

TWIST 2. Renata's logs show that she obeyed a Ceres Mutual directive to park Lantern and coat it with spoil, and that she formally warned the coating would change the rock's thermal behaviour. The Compact closed her warning and blamed her instead for an unrelated docking mishap. Ceres created its own doomsday rock, and Vesta is quietly saving Ceres from it. Piq's whole loyalty inverts: the institution she serves buried the truth and destroyed Teo's mother to do it. Teo holds very still while Piq reads aloud the parts Teo cannot. Ends: Piq traces the sanitized file's authorising signature. It is a board-level initial set she cannot identify.

There is grief and tenderness between Piq and Teo, and Piq admits she is no longer sure whom she works for. Teo admits she cannot model what she feels and that this frightens her. The captain announces a water leak and imposes rations, and the ship's mass budget tightens around everyone. A clump of messages arrives through the relay: eight from Piq's mother and one from Marisol reading 'QO coast nominal'. Distracted, Piq misses it in the pile. Ends: Ruiz identifies Piq as the Ceres assessor, using her dish requests and the hearing records, and invokes ship's law to have her confined.

Piq is confined to her cabin, and the captain refuses to take sides. Ostlund, now fiercely loyal, smuggles notes to her inside wedding paperwork, and the comedy of his forms is laced with real stakes. Teo visits, and through the open hatch they share their first kiss, honest and late. Together they finally parse 'QO coast nominal': something launched is now coasting. Teo re-reduces Juniper's 'ghost' images and finds a dim, dark object on the Ceres–Vesta line. Ends: Piq lines up the object's back-solved launch time against the moment her retraction left the ship, and the numbers do not fall the way she needs them to.

TWIST 3. Comedy is withdrawn from here through Chapter 17 except for small human moments. The Pallas batch schedule, the clumped messages and the ghost smudge fall into place. Her retraction sat in the relay's low-priority queue for 11 hours and reached Ceres after the decision window had closed, so the Quiet Option was launched on her first report. Nobody lied: Marisol acted correctly on what she had, and 'Proceeding' meant proceeding with launch. The interceptor is a dark kinetic penetrator, radio-silent so it cannot be spoofed and abortable only by an optical key at close range. Its target is the driver. Without the driver's final shots, Lantern hits Ceres. Piq's impatience, her decisiveness, did this. Ends: the interceptor reaches Vesta in 26 days, and Patience flies past in 22.

The only key within reach is Piq's notary seal. The only vehicle is the Gannet, and its propellant is the ship's water. The captain refuses: the leak has already cut the budget, and she will not trade shielding for one gamble. The passengers, led by Ostlund and the newlyweds Halvard and Mei-Lin, donate their water rations, and Juniper adds her winnings. Ruiz moves to block the launch until Piq points out that a destroyed driver costs Mars its leverage too, so he stands aside for the wrong reason. Teo insists on flying the intercept, knowing that leaving Patience means not returning for years, and she makes a choice she cannot model. A solar particle event is forecast. Launch. Ends: the event arrives early.

In the Gannet, every kilogram of water they burn is a kilogram less shielding. Teo calculates radiation dose against delta-v in real time while Piq keeps her talking, and they say true things because there is no time left to say them later. A small, tired joke releases pressure without breaking the suspense. Ends: they acquire the interceptor optically, and it is not where it should be.

The interceptor has made a terminal correction. They overburn and take more dose. At 900 km the seal's handshake fails, because its clock drift, flagged by Ostlund in Chapter 2, throws off the timing window. Piq works out the offset and corrects for it with the light-delay arithmetic Teo taught her. The abort succeeds. Ends: the Gannet no longer has the propellant to return to Patience and is falling toward Vesta in the driver's final firing window.

The chapter opens taut and closes warm. Vell fires the last rounds, and Teo's tracking confirms Lantern is deflected clear of Ceres. A Vesta tug captures the Gannet. Vell publicly confesses the deflection campaign and the cover-up he uncovered, accepts arrest by Mars, and commits Vesta to repaying Patience's water in full. Ruiz places the true sequence of events on the record honestly, and his report names Piq. Teo's final track shows a small fragment shed by the last impact, which she names Wick; its orbit cannot yet be determined. In the aftermath on Vesta, Piq notarizes Renata's logs into the public record, clearing her name, and Vell's team credits Juniper as an observer while she collects on the pool. Over a light-delayed link from Patience, Ostlund officiates Halvard and Mei-Lin's vow renewal, and Piq co-signs the certificate from Vesta. Piq finally sends her mother something true: she has fallen in love. Marisol's message arrives with apology, thanks and a summons to the Hygiea Water Accord talks at Mars, and promises an 'internal' inquiry into the board initials. The reply from Piq's mother arrives in a clump of eleven messages, the last of which simply says 'Bring her home.' Piq and Teo both carry radiation dose and are stranded nine months from the next transfer window, with inquiries, Martian jurisdiction and ruined careers ahead. They choose each other plainly and without any cover. Final image: two women watching Ceres, a bright point 31 light-minutes away, talking about what they will say when they get there.

notes:
CH1 SUMMARY (Day 1 aboard Patience): Piq boards via a Mars-flyby taxi (9-day trip) at the hub. Her duffel weighs 34.1 kg against a 20 kg allowance, so she is 14.1 kg over, with a 100 g tolerance. Teo (introduced as Teodora Anselm, trajectory & mass) measures her in the spring-mounted inertial-mass chair at 68.4 kg (registration said 69). Option 1, pay freight, would cost about a month of Piq's real salary. Option 2: wear it. The tariff envelope is 95 kg per passenger, body plus worn items, and anything worn when the manifest closes at 2200 ship's time is logged as personal effects. Piq wears everything. Re-weigh: bag 19.8 kg, body+effects 82.6 kg. Teo logs the missing 100 g as evaporative sweat ('It'll probably end up in a tomato'). Teo never smiles on duty ('Mass is a sincere subject') and warns Piq to stand slowly in the ring. Piq finds her quietly amused and attractive. At ring orientation (sector 4), purser/steward Okafor (shaved head, cheerful) has everyone stand. Piq, top-heavy in layers, staggers from Coriolis, sits down hard and gets applause as a 'perfect demonstration.' Okafor's key lines: water is drink, plants and sun-shielding all at once; report leaks. The storm shelter is in the hub with water-tank walls; drills are announced, real events are not. The chapel doubles as courtroom and as Thursday quiz night. The Gannet is the ship's taxi, stencilled PLEASE DO NOT LEAN ON THE GANNET (a running joke). Piq's cabin: Ring 2 / 4-17, outer deck of spoke two, 2x3 m. She opens Marisol's brief with the seal. Then Mei-Lin Okoro (small, neat, black hair pinned up, fiercely organized) and Halvard Brekke (2 m tall, red beard, stooped and gentle) arrive at about 18:31, roughly 5.5 hours after boarding. They give her a potted tomato plant and ask her to marry them in free fall in the hub before Vesta. They met in free fall on a tug and have been engaged 4 years. They had gone to Ostlund first, who gave them 11 forms and an 8-week 'orbital humility' course with an exam. Piq accepts, though she has never officiated a wedding, and promises 'there is always paperwork.' Chapter ends with her opening the Celebrant's Forms and Liturgies to 'Chapter One: Before You Begin.'

ESTABLISHED FACTS:
- Piq: 34, Ceres-born. 11 years in the Assessment Office (officially nonexistent). Past covers: freight clerk at Pallas, hydroponics inspector at Hygiea, pressure-suit buyer at a Juno scrapyard. Her notary/celebrant commission was earned at 23 (she passed narrowly; the swearing registrar called her 'my dear') and is renewed every 3 years. She has notarized 412 documents and never married anyone. Her reviews say 'decisive', 'instinctive' and always 'impatient'. She did 8 weeks of centrifuge conditioning at the Mars Academy. Her mother on Ceres sends long chatty messages. She has never had a desk or a home under her own name. Her directory listing reads 'Notary Public & Marriage Celebrant, Ceres Registry. Commissions accepted' (the Registry template added the last part; she left it).
- Seal: brass and black glass, palm-sized, inscribed CERES REGISTRY—NOTARIUS PUBLICUS—PER FIDEM. It embosses and prints a timestamp plus commission number in black dots. The glass chip at its centre hides an optical key whose pattern shifts every few seconds by an internal clock only Compact engineers can read. It unlocks Compact files on her slate. (Clock-drift clue is due in Ch2.) She keeps it in her inner jacket pocket.
- Marisol's brief (recorded before departure; terse, signed 'M.', addresses Piq as 'P.'): flyby in 140 days at 40,000 km closest approach. The rail is estimated at 9 km, electromagnetic, and Mars has said nothing about it. Task: image, characterize, confirm or deny a threat to Ceres. Her rules: 'Don't send what you can't stand behind. Don't be clever.' A clean result earns Piq the Ceres desk, which Marisol will sign herself. Attachments: orbits, one useless grainy image, standing instructions, a note on Mars personnel likely aboard.
- Ship: Patience is 1.2 km long with 3 spokes, a sunward shield and dishes. The trip to Ceres approach takes about 5 months. The ring has hydroponics behind glass (violet lamps, tomato smell, condensation), galley, gym and chapel. The hub has docks, mass office, telescope club and shelter. Showers are timed and metered; grey water goes to hydroponics; no scented soap. Supper is at 1900. About 20 new arrivals came on Piq's taxi.
- Teo: about 38 (Piq guessed ~40), close-cropped dark hair going silver, shorter and solider than Piq, raised in real gravity. She wears a faded embroidered patch of a tug pulling a rock (her mother's; not yet explained). Piq does not yet call her 'Teo'.
- Directory: Mars Republic attaché bound for Hygiea (Ruiz, not yet met), Br. L. Ostlund of the Fellowship of the Long Orbit (ceremonies require 8 weeks' notice plus preparatory forms), a family with 5 children, three ice-prospectors, a Pallas student, two elderly men in matching sweaters, and others. Juniper's telescope club meets in the hub observatory ('all welcome, ask for Juniper'); Piq has calendared it.

WHO KNOWS WHAT: No one aboard knows Piq is an assessor. Ostlund presumably does not yet know of her. Halvard and Mei-Lin think she is an experienced celebrant.

OPEN THREADS: The manifest closes at 2200 and Piq stays layered until then. Wedding paperwork is due tomorrow, and she must learn celebrant procedure. Ostlund's audit is coming. Juniper's club. Ruiz's dinner introduction (Ch2). Mother's message clumps via the Pallas Relay (Ch2). Seal clock drift (Ch2). Dish time rationing (Ch2).
